clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old male presented with weakness, a fall, and a right-sided facial droop, with a history of hyperglycemia and recent SARS-CoV-2 infection. Initial non-contrast CT scan demonstrated advanced sinusitis. Subsequent CTA showed advanced sinusitis, abnormal gas in several foci in the skull base, left occipital condyle, and soft tissues adjacent to the clivus. These radiological findings, along with fiberoptic nasal endoscopy demonstrating sinusitis, were interpreted as 'radiological findings of SBO' (Skull Base Osteomyelitis), increasing suspicion for invasive sinusitis due to mucormycosis. Pathological findings from biopsy confirmed non-septate branching hyphae, indicative of potential mucormycosis from fungal infiltration. Endoscopic debridement further demonstrated Mucor on the carotid wall. The combination of confirmed mucormycosis and radiological evidence of skull base osteomyelitis, with involvement adjacent to the clivus, supports the final diagnosis.
